extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting manuscripts to The Review of Economic Studies (economics researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed submission and formatting policies for authors preparing new or revised manuscripts for The Review of Economic Studies, including fees, editorial conflicts, data availability, length and formatting requirements, and rules for resubmission and comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission fee amount and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: With effect from 1 July 2023, the submission fee is USD 200 for new submissions. There is a reduced submission fee of USD 120 if each and every author meets at least one of the following conditions: (i) is a current student, (ii) is within six years of completing their PhD, or (iii) resides in a low- or middle-income economy (according to the World Bank classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting evidence with links to authors’ websites or CVs is required at the time of submission. Resubmissions are not subject to this fee, except for ‘reject and resubmits’, which are subject to the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission fee does not guarantee full review
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of the submission fee does not guarantee that a full review process is going to be carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors first review each manuscript to ensure it is appropriate for the journal and has a sufficiently high chance of receiving a favorable review; papers judged inappropriate may be returned without sending to outside referees. The submission and fee represent a contract between RESL and the individual making the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole submission / prior publication prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are evaluated on the understanding that they have been submitted solely to The Review of Economic Studies and that they have not been previously published or previously accepted for publication in other scientific journals either in whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should submit new and revised manuscripts online at the specified submission portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial assignment and conflict of interest rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review adopts strict guidelines to avoid professional conflicts of interest in allocation of submissions to managing editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managing editors are not allowed to handle submissions by advisors, advisees, current colleagues at the same institution (regardless of department), coauthors (with a 10 year grace period), family members, or any other authors whose personal or professional ties may call into question integrity. Managing Editors must disclose and discuss any assignment that might violate the guidelines; the team may reassign papers when there are concerns. These allocations cannot be appealed by submitting authors, nor will managing editors discuss rationale. Submitting authors may suggest editorial assignment only if compatible with workload/expertise and not violating conflict rules. Managing editors and the Chair have refrained from submitting their own papers to the Review during their editorial term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and code availability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of accepted papers that contain empirical work, numerical simulations, or experimental work must in principle make available to the journal any data, programs, and details for the computations necessary for replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are strongly advised to read the Data Availability Policy before submission. The Review endorses DCAS (Data and Code Availability Standard) v1.0 and is compatible with DCAS. Requests for exemptions should be clearly stated in the cover letter when the article is first submitted; exemptions will be reviewed by the Managing Editors and the Data Editor and will not be considered later in the review/publication process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: With effect from 1 July 2022, papers should be under 45 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes title page, tables, figures, references and appendices. In exceptional circumstances longer papers may be allowed, but authors should provide compelling reasons and request an exception prior to submission (direct such requests to the named editor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Online appendix policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may include an appendix intended for online publication only, clearly labeled 'Online Appendix'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online appendix should not exceed 30 pages (same font and spacing requirements as the manuscript). Online appendices are for additional results and robustness analyses that are not central to the main paper. The main paper should be self-contained and should encompass proofs of key results, or at least a sketch of the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting: paper size, margins, spacing, font, pagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted manuscripts should be formatted for paper of standard size with margins of at least 1 inch on all sides, 1-1/2 spaced text in 12-point font, and pages should be numbered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References and footnotes can be single-spaced. The 12pt font applies to the entire manuscript, including appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single PDF submission and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should upload a single PDF file containing the complete manuscript (title page, abstract, text, figures and tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to figure file size constraints, separate files for figures may be submitted only if strictly necessary; the location of these figures should be indicated in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page contents and abstract length
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should be short, specific and informative. The first name, initial(s), and surname of each author should be followed by department, institution, city with postcode, and country. The fax, telephone number and Email address of the corresponding author should also be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is editorial policy to list only one author for correspondence. Any changes of address may be given next to the Affiliations or Acknowledgements. An abstract of no more than 150 words as well as keywords should be included with all submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-standard abbreviations should be defined at the first occurrence and introduced only where multiple use is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not use abbreviations in headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements placement and separation of funding/conflict statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgements and details of non-financial support must be included at the end of the text before references and not in footnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal acknowledgements should precede those of institutions or agencies. Acknowledgement of funding bodies and declarations regarding conflict of interest should be given in separate Funding and Conflict of interest sections, respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables formatting and content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables should be accompanied by a title, and footnotes where necessary, and should be numbered consecutively using Arabic numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units should be given in parentheses at the top of each column and not repeated in each line. Avoid overcrowding and excessive words. The format should be in keeping with the journal: in particular, vertical lines, coloured text and shading should not be used. Ensure data in tables are correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spell-check recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that authors spell-check all files before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may include files for any other supplementary material to be submitted with the manuscript only where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission and revise-and-resubmit policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmissions: the editorial team reserves the right to treat 'revise and resubmit' papers as new submissions after one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are not allowed to submit revisions of manuscripts that have been previously rejected unless they are explicitly invited to resubmit by an editor. Resubmissions are not subject to the submission fee, except for 'reject and resubmits', which are subject to the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for comments on previously published REStud papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review accepts comments on papers previously published in the journal only if (1) there is a factual mistake in the original paper; and (2) this mistake substantially affects the results of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors of comments should submit through the regular route and indicate in the cover letter that the manuscript is a comment. The submission fee for comments is the same as for any other submitted papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment/fee contractual terms and tax treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission and fee represent a contract between RESL and the individual making the submission, not any institution that may employ them; the payment does not constitute consultancy fees or advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission fee charged is inclusive of all taxes that RESL will have to pay in the UK. No repayment of any tax element of the submission fee will be made to the submitter or to his/her agent or any institution that the submitter seeks to seek reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' right to return non-compliant manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editors reserve the right to return manuscripts that are not in accordance with these instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that main paper be self-contained
rubrics_metrics.description: The main paper should be self-contained and should thus also encompass proofs of key results, or at least a sketch of the argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online appendices are for additional results and robustness analyses that are not central to the main paper; key proofs belong (or sketched) in main paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice to read linked policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly advised to read the Data Availability Policy before making a submission and to consult Copyright, Licence and Open Access information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with Data Availability Policy terms could delay or prevent publication.
